title: Prepare Market Data for Forecasting with NVIDIA Megatron Core | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA published a Megatron-LM example that turns intraday market-bar Parquet data into patched, model-ready tensors and trains transformer models to forecast returns and trading volume across multiple horizons. The pipeline emphasizes leakage control (date splits, embargo, train-only target statistics) and a fixed data interface so quants can swap in their own architectures.

insights.claim: NVIDIA added a financial time-series example to Megatron-LM that preprocesses intraday market bars and trains a transformer to forecast returns and trading volume at multiple horizons using Megatron Core's distributed training loop.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is courting capital-markets firms to train their own forecasting foundation models on GPU clusters, expanding FSI compute demand.
insights.locator: NVIDIA Megatron Core is an open-source library

insights.claim: The Megatron financial pipeline keeps price and volume as continuous features via a learned patch embedding rather than converting market values into text tokens.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: Signals the finance-foundation-model approach favored by NVIDIA is time-series transformers, not LLMs reading numbers as text.

insights.claim: A single shared forecasting model can be trained across many instruments, with each window tagged by instrument ID so the model learns instrument-specific behavior within shared parameters.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: Cross-asset pooled models are the scaling path for market forecasting, favoring firms with broad data and compute.
insights.locator: A common data interface supports training

insights.claim: The preprocessing script groups consecutive bars into patches that act as tokens, e.g. eight bars per patch and 32 patches per window give 256 observations in 32 model positions, each patch carrying its intraday session position.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: Practical recipe for tokenizing tick/bar data for transformers.

insights.claim: Each training window carries targets for every context position, so one forward pass yields forecasts across the whole context; targets can be point (a future step) or cumulative (summed log return and total volume), with volume on a log scale.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: Dense per-position targets improve training efficiency for causal forecasting models.

insights.claim: The example forecasts at horizons of 1, 2, 5 and 15 steps on 390 time units per day, with within-day log returns derived by the script so the overnight gap never enters the inputs.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: Configured for one-minute US-session-style bars; useful template for short-horizon execution research.

insights.claim: The pipeline splits data by date, keeps a window only if its full context and longest-horizon future fall in one split, applies an embargo of trading days before validation, and checks context patches do not overlap across splits to prevent forward-looking bias.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: Embedding leakage controls in the default tooling reduces the most common failure in ML backtests.

insights.claim: Per-horizon target normalization statistics are computed from the training split only, so future evaluation data never determines target scaling used in training.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: A subtle look-ahead source many quant ML pipelines get wrong.

insights.claim: Preprocessing writes train.pt, val.pt, test.pt and meta.pt tensors offline so Parquet parsing and target construction stay outside the training loop, and a memory-mapped loader has rank zero in each tensor-parallel group read and broadcast microbatches.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: Removes data I/O as a GPU-utilization bottleneck when scaling market models across GPUs.
insights.locator: Efficient data loading for distributed training

insights.claim: The data layer is decoupled from the model: any MegatronModule accepting patches, instrument IDs and patch time-of-day and returning return and volshare tensors can replace the small example model.
insights.speaker: Liana Mikaelyan
insights.so_what: Lowers the barrier for quant teams to plug proprietary architectures into NVIDIA's training stack.
